voiceover: You push your project and the upload takes forever. You committed node modules, a folder with thousands of other people's files. You don't need to. Your package.json lists what the project needs, and npm install rebuilds the folder anywhere. Add node modules to a file called .gitignore, and git skips it from then on. Already committed it? Remove it from tracking, then commit again. Send this to whoever pushed node modules.

scenes.text: Why is your repo so huge?

scenes.verdict: commit the recipe, not the folder

scenes.title: .gitignore
lines: // git skips these from now on

captions.instagram:
